ground_truth.description: The single-task check is instructed to use search(..., limit=50) and to rely on the vector-ranking bias from appending 'task_id=<N>' to the query to surface the one target record. On a busy project with more than ~50 'stage1_flag_suppression' records, embeddings do not reliably rank an exact task_id token match into the top 50 (numeric task_id tokens are weakly discriminated by the embedding, and the dominant term 'stage1_flag_suppression' is shared by every record), so the authoritative suppression record can fall below the cutoff and be missed. The reader then concludes 'no suppression in effect' and emits a flag that should have been suppressed — exactly the false-negative (review-passed-but-escalation-created) failure this task was flagged for. The post-processor's own sweep uses limit=501 precisely to avoid this; capping the reader's check at 50 reintroduces the miss.

On search error/timeout the prompt directs the reader to treat suppression as not-in-effect and emit the flag (fail-open with respect to suppression). It justifies this as mirroring filter_suppressed's 'conservative pass-through', but pass-through in the post-processor keeps flags for the opposite reason; here it means an intentionally suppressed task can get a flag emitted on a transient search failure, which is the same false-negative direction and relies entirely on the downstream post-processor still catching it.

task.title: Harden Stage 1 suppression-check prompt: search params, error semantics, task_id type
task.description:
Three small but compounding correctness gaps in the new "Flag Suppression Check" section of STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT:

1. Search call has no categories/stores/limit. Default limit=10 in memory_service.search means a busy project's suppression record can rank outside top 10 and be silently missed.
2. No guidance for search-error/timeout. Neighboring "Terminal-State Pre-Check Discipline" handles this explicitly; this section will improvise differently across runs.
3. metadata.task_id is documented as integer with strict `==` comparison. Mem0 metadata round-trips through JSON and writers in this codebase have stored task_id as both int and str — same bug class that previously bit flag dedup.
task.details:
Origin: review suggestions 2, 3, 4 (reviewer_comprehensive) on task 1169.

Location: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/stage1.py:234-257

Concrete edits:
- Replace the search instruction with: `search(query="stage1_flag_suppression task_id=<N>", project_id=..., categories=['observations_and_summaries'], stores=['mem0'], limit=50)`. Including task_id in the query string also helps vector ranking.
- Add an explicit clause for error/timeout — recommended: "If the suppression search returns an error or times out, treat suppression as not-in-effect and proceed with normal flag emission; record the search failure in your cycle summary so operators can re-check." (Pick this OR the conservative alternative; commit to one and justify in a sentence.)
- Pin task_id type: either declare "writers MUST store metadata.task_id as a string; readers compare as strings" OR change the comparison instruction to coerce both sides: `str(result.metadata.get('task_id')) == str(target_task_id)`. Mirror the choice in any producer code (see sibling producer task).

If the post-processor enforcement task lands first, several of these may shift: in that case, only items 2 and 3 still apply to whatever code runs the search.
